hero.headline: Vero Beach group collects earthquake relief supplies for Venezuela through Saturday
hero.teaser: Latinas Nexus Network in Vero Beach is hosting a Venezuela Earthquake Relief Drive, collecting essential supplies to ship directly to communities devastated by a massive earthquake in Venezuela.
hero.body:
A Vero Beach organization is gathering donations for Venezuelan communities devastated by a powerful earthquake, with organizers emphasizing the urgency of the relief effort. Latinas Nexus Network is hosting the Venezuela Earthquake Relief Drive to collect essential supplies for shipment to affected areas. The initiative is being led by founders Lourana Navarro and Juliana Marino, along with Heidi Ramirez.

Navarro, who was born in Venezuela and now lives in Vero Beach, said her immediate family in Caracas is safe, but communities surrounding the capital have suffered severe losses. She described the scale of the disaster as immense. "When I started seeing the magnitude and that it was a 7.5, I really got scared," Navarro said. She emphasized that recovery will take an extended period. "Seeing the devastation, I know this is going to take decades to recover. We as a country don't have the resources," she said. Marino stressed the organization's commitment to directing assistance effectively. "From here, the only thing that I can do is do our best to come together and help them and find different resources so we can get it directly to the people and bring the help that they need," Marino said.

The organizers are partnering with Global Empowerment Mission to transport collected supplies to Venezuela, guaranteeing that 100 percent of donations will go through verified humanitarian relief channels. Marino noted the scale of need is substantial. "We're talking hundreds of thousands of people that are in need right now," she said. Both organizers highlighted the most critical shortages facing survivors. "I can tell you that the worst is the food and the place to sleep, to take a bath, they don't have that right now," Navarro said. The relief drive welcomes participation from all community members, not exclusively the Hispanic population. "We are asking not just the Hispanic community, we are asking everyone. They really need us," the founders said.

The organization is collecting powder Gatorade, non-perishable food, baby formula and baby food, diapers in all sizes, baby wipes, feminine hygiene products, soap, shampoo, toothbrushes and toothpaste, rain boots, toilet paper, blankets, sleeping bags with batteries, flashlights and batteries, heavy duty garbage bags, first aid kits, bandages and gauze, hand sanitizer, cleaning supplies, face masks, nitrile gloves, and plastic bins with lids. Donations can be dropped off at 684 Old Dixie Highway, Vero Beach, FL 32962. The collection runs through Saturday, June 27, 2026, from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. To reach the organizers, contact Lourana Navarro at 954-205-0700, Juliana Marino at 772-913-0805, or Heidi Ramirez at 772-213-2747.

cards.headline: DeSantis signs stablecoin framework and crypto kiosk fraud protections into Florida law
cards.teaser: Gov.
cards.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis signed three bills Friday that directly affect Florida's financial services sector and the treatment of money. CS/CS/HB 175 brings stablecoins under state regulation in line with the federal Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for U.S. Stablecoins Act, known as the GENIUS Act. The Office of Financial Regulation will determine whether an entity qualifies as a qualified payment stablecoin issuer by issuing a money services business license or, for trust companies, granting a certificate of approval. Under the law, stablecoins can be used for financial settlement with their value pegged at a fixed one-to-one rate of exchange with the U.S. dollar. The bill takes effect in October.

CS/CS/SB 1568 establishes the Florida Stablecoin Pilot Program within the Department of Financial Services, allowing applicants and licensees to voluntarily pay licensing, registration, application and renewal fees using approved stablecoins. The department will determine which stablecoins qualify based on strict financial safeguards, such as being fully backed by reserve assets worth at least $1 billion. DFS is authorized to maintain a state-designated digital wallet to convert stablecoin payments into U.S. dollars. HB 505 brings virtual currency kiosk operators under state money transmitter licensing rules, requiring registration with OFR and displaying fraud warnings on initial screens. Transaction limits are capped at $2,000 daily for new users and $10,000 for established customers.

cards.headline: Two people killed in head-on crash on Allapattah Road in Indiantown
cards.body:
Two people were killed in a head-on crash Saturday morning on Allapattah Road near Martin Highway in Indiantown. The crash occurred around 6:30 a.m. at 8113 SW Allapattah Road, also known as the Allapattah S-Curve, according to the Martin County Sheriff's Office.

Allapattah Road was blocked for about six hours while the Florida Highway Patrol processed the scene. The Martin County Sheriff's Office reported the crash and coordinated the road closure with state troopers.

The road reopened Saturday afternoon after investigators finished documenting the crash scene. The Florida Highway Patrol is handling the investigation into the collision.

The Allapattah S-Curve is a known dangerous section of roadway in western Martin County. The identities of the two people killed have not been released by authorities.

cards.headline: Secretary of State Marco Rubio announces Israel-Lebanon framework agreement in Washington
cards.teaser: The framework establishes a process for dismantling Hezbollah and for Lebanon to regain territory taken by Israeli forces, with the U.S. committing $100 million in humanitarian assistance.
cards.body:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio joined Israel and Lebanon's ambassadors to the U.S. Friday to announce a framework agreement described as a first step toward peace following months of conflict between Israel and the Lebanese militant group Hezbollah. The agreement does not include Hezbollah and prompted one of the group's officials in Lebanon to warn of civil war. The State Department said the framework establishes a process for dismantling Hezbollah and for Lebanon to regain territory taken by Israeli forces as they battled the militant group. The U.S. will facilitate a newly created Military Coordination Group for Lebanon to implement the framework while committing $100 million in humanitarian assistance.

The agreement was signed in Washington by Yechiel Leiter, the Israeli ambassador to the United States, and Nada Hamadeh Moawad, the Lebanese ambassador to the United States. Leiter said the final destination of the framework is peace between the two countries and expressed hopes for normalized relations, stating Israel wants Hezbollah disarmed and dismantled so it can withdraw and Lebanon can regain full sovereignty. Moawad said the framework is a first step toward restoring Lebanese sovereignty and territorial integrity, securing a permanent cessation of hostilities, enabling people to return to their land and allowing all Lebanese to live in peace, security and prosperity.

cards.headline: Vero Beach group launches Venezuela earthquake relief drive at Old Dixie Highway location
cards.body:
Latinas Nexus Network in Vero Beach is organizing a relief effort to help Venezuelan communities devastated by a recent 7.5 magnitude earthquake. The organization, founded by Lourana Navarro and Juliana Marino with assistance from Heidi Ramirez, is collecting essential supplies to send directly to affected areas. Navarro, who was born in Venezuela, said her own family in Caracas escaped injury, but neighboring communities suffered catastrophic losses. "Where it was, there is a lot of my family there, so when I started seeing the magnitude and that it was a 7.5, I really got scared," Navarro said. She emphasized the scope of the crisis, noting that recovery will require many years and resources beyond what the country currently has available.

The organizers are working with Global Empowerment Mission, a verified humanitarian organization, to ensure that collected donations reach people in need. Marino stressed the importance of getting supplies to the most vulnerable populations. "From here, the only thing that I can do is do our best to come together and help them and find different resources so we can get it directly to the people and bring the help that they need," Marino said. The founders promise that 100 percent of donated supplies will go through established relief channels rather than being diverted elsewhere. Both organizers highlighted the most pressing needs among survivors. "I can tell you that the worst is the food and the place to sleep — to take a bath — they don't have that right now," Navarro said. Marino added that hundreds of thousands of people currently need assistance.

The relief drive is accepting donations from all community members, not exclusively from the Hispanic population. "We are asking not just the Hispanic community, we are asking everyone. They really need us," the founders said. Items needed include powder Gatorade, non-perishable food, baby formula and baby food, diapers of all sizes, baby wipes, feminine hygiene products, soap, shampoo, toothbrushes and toothpaste, rain boots, toilet paper, blankets, sleeping bags with batteries, flashlights and batteries, heavy duty garbage bags, first aid kits, bandages and gauze, hand sanitizer, cleaning supplies, face masks, nitrile gloves, and plastic bins with lids.

Donations can be dropped off at 684 Old Dixie Highway in Vero Beach through Saturday, June 27, 2026, between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. Those interested in contributing can contact the organizers directly: Lourana Navarro at (954) 205-0700, Juliana Marino at (772) 913-0805, or Heidi Ramirez at (772) 213-2747.

cards.headline: Missing diver found dead near Fort Pierce Inlet after search off Avalon State Park
cards.teaser: A missing diver was found dead on the ocean floor Saturday afternoon in approximately 55 feet of water about six to seven miles north-northeast of the Fort Pierce Inlet.
cards.body:
The U.S. Coast Guard Station Fort Pierce received a Mayday call over VHF Channel 16 at approximately 11:30 a.m. Friday regarding a missing diver. Following the distress call, the Coast Guard notified the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission, which immediately deployed four vessels to assist in the search. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit had independently monitored the Mayday call and was already en route to assist. Aerial support was provided by both the Coast Guard and FWC during the search.

Responding units made contact with the vessel involved nearly due east of Avalon State Park, approximately 6 to 7 miles north-northeast of the Fort Pierce Inlet. At approximately 4:10 p.m., civilian divers who were friends of the missing diver entered the water and located the missing diver at the bottom of the ocean in approximately 55 feet of water. The diver was recovered and pronounced deceased. The deceased was transported to Coast Guard Station Fort Pierce. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Criminal Investigations Division is conducting the investigation into the circumstances surrounding the incident, which remains ongoing.

cards.headline: Alligator Alcatraz closes but environmental groups push for Everglades restoration
cards.teaser: Trailers are rolling out of the remote immigration detention center in the Everglades known as Alligator Alcatraz, but environmental advocates and members of the Miccosukee Tribe say the fight over the land is far from over.
cards.body:
The immigration detention center known as Alligator Alcatraz is being dismantled, but environmental advocates and the Miccosukee Tribe say the closure does not resolve damage to the Everglades. Environmental groups gathered at the facility's entrance Friday morning, arguing that high-intensity lighting, diesel generators, heavy paving and continuous traffic may have damaged critical habitat for endangered Florida panthers and other wildlife. Elise Bennett of the Center for Biological Diversity said the harm "has not been undone by the announcement of a closure." Eve Samples, executive director of Friends of the Everglades, called the facility "an obscene waste of taxpayer dollars, dollars to the tune of about a billion dollars." The group has a pending federal lawsuit against the facility.

Betty Osceola of the Miccosukee Tribe said the work is not finished "until all that infrastructure comes out." She said her tribe has a deep and personal connection to the landscape and believes the Miccosukee people are its rightful stewards. A recent proposal from Miami-Dade County's mayor would transfer the roughly 25,000-acre space to the National Park Service for conservation. Gov. Ron DeSantis said during a Thursday news conference that Alligator Alcatraz "fulfilled the role it was designed to serve" and the center was always intended to be short-lived.

cards.headline: Florida property tax restrictions tighten as November ballot amendment looms
cards.teaser: Gov. Ron DeSantis signed new laws tightening how cities, counties and special districts can raise property tax revenue, generally tying local governments closer to the rollback rate.
cards.body:
Governor Ron DeSantis signed new laws this week that tighten how cities, counties and special districts can raise property-tax revenue. The measures generally tie local governments closer to the rollback rate, the rate designed to bring in roughly the same property-tax revenue as the prior year, and require larger votes to go higher. Florida Chief Financial Officer Blaise Ingoglia said government at all levels needs to start thinking about spending cuts. Supporters call the changes taxpayer protection and say local governments have allowed budgets to grow too quickly as property values rise.

Local officials warn the new restrictions, combined with the proposed November constitutional amendment, could leave cities and counties with major budget holes. That amendment, appearing on the November ballot as Amendment 3, would expand homestead exemptions on non-school property taxes first to $150,000 in 2027, then to $250,000 in 2028. Backers say it would deliver meaningful relief to homeowners. Opponents warn the savings for some property owners could lead to service cuts, higher fees or tax shifts elsewhere. A new outside campaign is now urging voters to reject the amendment, adding another front to what is expected to be one of Florida's most closely watched ballot fights this fall.

cards.headline: New Common Ground Party named as Florida governor's race intensifies
cards.teaser: Orlando attorney John Morgan announced his new political party will be called the Common Ground Party, and its members will be known as Grounders.
cards.body:
Orlando attorney John Morgan's new political party has officially been named the Common Ground Party, with members to be known as "Grounders." The $100,000 naming contest drew more than 250 suggestions, and the prize money will be shared among those who proposed the winning name. Morgan said the effort is "worth a try to undo the gridlock, the hate, and all of the meanness that has fallen into politics on all sides," though he acknowledged uncertainty about whether it will succeed. He has positioned the party as an alternative for voters frustrated with both Democrats and Republicans.

However, significant challenges remain for the fledgling party. Questions persist about what the Common Ground Party's platform will be, whether it can secure ballot access, and whether the Grounders can establish themselves as a legitimate political force or become another short-lived third-party experiment in Florida politics. Meanwhile, Florida's Republican gubernatorial race continues to intensify ahead of the Aug. 18 primary, though candidates still have not appeared on a debate stage together. U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds remains the only Republican candidate meeting the party's debate criteria, while rivals Paul Renner, Lt. Jay Collins, and James Fishback continue calling for a head-to-head contest.

cards.headline: Republican governor candidates argue for debates as Donalds refuses
cards.teaser: U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds remains the only Republican candidate meeting the party's debate criteria, leaving rivals arguing voters deserve a head-to-head contest before the Aug. 18 primary.
cards.body:
Republican candidates Paul Renner, Lt. Gov. Jay Collins, and James Fishback are pushing for debates in the governor's race ahead of Florida's Aug. 18 primary, but frontrunner Byron Donalds has refused their calls. Renner criticized the debate process in a recent interview, suggesting internal party politics are protecting Donalds. Donalds, the only Republican candidate meeting the party's debate criteria, has rebuffed the requests. At a Florida Chamber press conference announcing their endorsement of his campaign, Donalds compared the governor's race to a job interview, saying "If I'm applying for a job, it's not my responsibility to help my competitor get a job interview." No debate has materialized even from local news outlets so far.

The race continues to accelerate through advertising instead. Collins announced a "multi-million dollar statewide" advertising blitz, while Donalds is planning a $20 million statewide ad buy through the primary. Fishback attempted to maintain momentum for his insurgent campaign by naming former South Florida police officer Sean Lozano as his running mate and deputy campaign manager. At the announcement in Tallahassee, Lozano stated, "We will not politely manage Florida's decline. We will stop it."

hero.headline: Missing diver found dead on ocean floor near Fort Pierce Inlet
hero.body:
Authorities are investigating the death of a diver who was found on the ocean floor Friday afternoon. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office responded after the U.S. Coast Guard Station Fort Pierce received a Mayday call at approximately 11:30 a.m. over VHF Channel 16 reporting a missing diver. The body was located in the Atlantic Ocean about 6 to 7 miles north-northeast of the Fort Pierce Inlet in approximately 55 feet of water.

Multiple agencies coordinated the response effort following the distress call. The Coast Guard notified the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission, which immediately deployed four vessels to assist with the search. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit also responded, having independently monitored the Mayday call and already being en route to help. Both the Coast Guard and FWC provided aerial support during the search operation. Responding units made contact with the vessel involved nearly due east of Avalon State Park.

At approximately 1 p.m., a group of civilian boaters who were friends of the missing diver departed from the Fort Pierce Inlet to aid in the search. At approximately 4:10 p.m., civilian divers entered the water and located the missing diver on the ocean floor. The diver was recovered and pronounced deceased at the scene. The body was then transported to Coast Guard Station Fort Pierce.

The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Criminal Investigations Division is conducting an investigation into the circumstances of the incident. The investigation remains ongoing as authorities work to determine what led to the diver's death. No additional information has been released at this time.

hero.headline: Boca Raton homeowner battles My Safe Florida Home grant delays despite completed storm upgrades
hero.teaser: Anne Bendel of West Boca Raton completed $8,000 in storm mitigation work to her home and submitted all required documentation for a My Safe Florida Home grant, .
hero.body:
Anne Bendel of West Boca Raton completed $8,000 in storm mitigation work on her home and submitted all required documentation for a My Safe Florida Home grant, but her application remains stuck in review. Bendel first contacted WPTV in May when her grant was held up by paperwork from her insurance company, which was eventually resolved. My Safe Florida Home then told her in May that her status was complete. One week later, representatives asked for more documentation: a permit of completion for a large impact window. After she provided it, questions arose about dates, sending her application back under review. Bendel says she has completed the work, obtained the permits, and secured the required insurance.

Bendel describes herself as persistent and thorough but says the grant process has pushed her to her limits. She handles the entire process on her phone without a computer and has no one to help her. The My Safe Florida Home program provides grants of up to $10,000 to help homeowners across the state fortify homes against storms and earn insurance discounts. Bendel questions whether the program is being fair, noting that each time she completes a task, representatives seem to find another requirement. WPTV has contacted the Florida Department of Financial Services in Tallahassee about her case and the status of her grant. Bendel says her confidence in the program's promises is being shaken as she waits to see if she will receive any grant money.

cards.headline: Immigration detainees from closed Alligator Alcatraz scattered to facilities across U.S.
cards.teaser: Detainees from the closed Everglades immigration facility have been moved to Louisiana, Texas, New Mexico, and as far as Tacoma, Washington, creating challenges for families and immigration attorneys fighting for bonds and residency.
cards.body:
Immigration attorney Richard Hujber said detainees from the closed Alligator Alcatraz facility in the Florida Everglades have been scattered to facilities in Louisiana, Texas, New Mexico, and Tacoma, Washington. According to Hujber, the relocations create massive challenges when fighting for bonds and navigating immigration law because different laws apply in different circuit courts across the country. With bond now out of reach for some detainees, they face the difficult decision of whether to continue fighting toward residency or asylum or give up and self-deport.

Gov. Ron DeSantis reported that roughly 21,000 people have been deported from the facility since it opened nearly a year ago. The closure brought mixed results for detainees, including Anna Maria Hernandez's cousin, who was released just before Alligator Alcatraz shut down and is now under an order of supervision that allows him to drive, work, and live in the U.S. Hujber acknowledged the fight is not easy and ultimately depends on the detainees themselves. The Baker County facility in North Florida remains operational.

cards.headline: Environmental groups and Miccosukee Tribe continue fight over Alligator Alcatraz Everglades site
cards.teaser: Trailers are rolling out of the closed immigration detention center in the Everglades, but environmental advocates and members of the Miccosukee Tribe say the fight over the land and damage to critical wildlife habitat is far from over.
cards.body:
Trailers are rolling out of the remote immigration detention center in the Everglades known as Alligator Alcatraz, but environmental advocates and members of the Miccosukee Tribe say the closure does not end their fight over the land. Betty Osceola of the Miccosukee Tribe said the work is not finished until all infrastructure is removed. Environmental advocates say high-intensity lighting, diesel generators, heavy paving and continuous traffic may have damaged critical habitat for endangered Florida panthers and other wildlife. Eve Samples, executive director of Friends of the Everglades, called the facility an obscene waste of taxpayer dollars, totaling about a billion dollars, and an abuse of the Everglades. The group has a pending federal lawsuit against the facility.

The question of what happens to the roughly 25,000-acre space remains unresolved. A recent proposal from Miami-Dade County's mayor would transfer the land to the National Park Service for conservation. However, Osceola said she does not trust government agencies to protect the land and believes the Miccosukee people are its rightful stewards, noting her family has been foraging for food and living on the landscape for generations. Ron DeSantis said the center accomplished what it was built to do and was always intended to be short-lived.

cards.headline: Former Haitian national team players mentor youth soccer players in Boca Raton
cards.teaser: Former members of the Haitian national soccer team spent time in Boca Raton this week mentoring the next generation of players at the L'Union Fait La Force Training Center, offering a pathway to the youth national team.
cards.body:
Former members of the Haitian national soccer team mentored young players in Boca Raton this week, just days after a Wednesday night match against Morocco. Nohe Chevry, one of the participants, moved to Palm Beach County with his family in 2022 due to safety concerns as unrest grew in Haiti. Soccer served as a safe haven for Chevry's family during that difficult period. After relocating, finding a local soccer team became a top priority, leading Chevry to the L'Union Fait La Force Training Center. "It's a great opportunity to learn; they've been through all of the soccer stuff, pro contracts, so they can teach us, and it's really kind of them to do that," Chevry said.

L'Union Fait La Force is a premier soccer development program run by former Haitian National Team members, including former team captain Jean-Marc Alexandre, an Atlantic High School and Lynn University graduate who was a member of Real Salt Lake's 2009 MLS Cup-winning team. "The whole purpose of this camp is to give these kids a pathway to the youth national team, being that they're not living in Haiti, so we give opportunities to the next generation," Alexandre said. The organization is hosting a clinic from June 25-28 teaching top-level Haitian soccer players the sport. Participant Luis Etienne said the opportunity could provide exposure for the national team, while Chevry expressed ambitions to play in the World Cup.

cards.headline: Lucky Shuck in Jupiter featured in Where's Walter segment
cards.teaser: Walter visited the Lucky Shuck in Jupiter, a waterfront restaurant founded by a professional athlete that serves about 4,000 oysters per week and can be reached by car or boat.
cards.body:
Walter's first "Where's Walter" adventure led him to the Lucky Shuck in Jupiter, a hidden gem founded by a professional athlete. Shining a Light reporter TA Walker joined the visit, sharing that the restaurant holds special meaning for him as the location of his first date with his now-husband, Charlie. Chef John, who has worked there since the restaurant's inception, guided them through the oyster selection, which features about five different types daily. The house specialty is Jemma's Pearls, named in honor of Joe Namath's granddaughter and given to the football legend for his birthday.

The restaurant's oyster volume is substantial, going through approximately 40 cases per week, with each case containing roughly 100 oysters, totaling 4,000 oysters. Diners can arrive by boat and watch vessels drift by while enjoying their meal, creating an experience that showcases South Florida's waterfront dining atmosphere. This inaugural "Where's Walter" adventure kicks off a weekly series that will explore new corners of the area to uncover hidden treasures in the community.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce Florida Highwaymen Museum featured in America 250 Road Trip celebration
hero.teaser: The Florida Highwaymen Museum in Fort Pierce, which opened this year, is part of festivities celebrating the nation's 250th birthday.
hero.body:
The Florida Highwaymen Museum, which opened this year in Fort Pierce, is a featured stop on the America 250 Road Trip celebrating the nation's 250th birthday. The city announced the designation on its Facebook page this week. The museum celebrates 26 Black artists who began painting in the 1950s, creating bold, colorful landscapes of Florida's untouched beauty and selling them along the roadside when segregation kept them out of traditional galleries. Located at 1234 Avenue D, the museum is the nation's only one with exhibitions that include paintings from each of the 26 renowned Highwaymen artists.

The museum operates on a seasonal schedule. During summer months from June 16 to July 31, it is open Saturday and Sunday from noon to 4 p.m. The museum will close in August and reopen in September with a new exhibit. Fall and spring hours, beginning September 1 and running through June 15, will be expanded.

cards.headline: SoFlo Market brings Independence Day celebration to Boca Raton City Hall on July 4
cards.teaser: The popular SoFlo Market will turn Boca Raton City Hall into a patriotic celebration this Independence Day with family activities, local vendors and gourmet food.
cards.body:
The SoFlo Market will celebrate Independence Day at Boca Raton City Hall on Saturday, July 4 from 11 a.m. to 5 p.m. at 201 West Palmetto Park Road. The free event features a kids' parade, DJ, unique vendors and gourmet food. Founder and organizer Tatiana Freitas said the market's mission is to uplift small local businesses and bring the community together. The first 20 children through the gate will receive a free gift.

Family entertainment includes face painting, a foggy bubble station, mini golf and balloon twisting alongside handmade crafts and desserts. A live appearance by the SoFlo Market's flamingo mascot is planned. Boca Raton firefighters and police officers have been invited to share the day with residents. Kyle, Freitas' son, and Eddie, her husband, are part of the organizing team. Electricity will be powered by generators on site, and the event's Instagram, TikTok, Facebook and YouTube channels will feature behind-the-scenes clips and photos throughout the day.

cards.headline: West Boca Raton homeowner faces new hurdles in My Safe Florida Home grant despite completed work
cards.teaser: Anne Bendel says her efforts to receive a promised grant from the state to fix up her home keep facing one hurdle after another.
cards.body:
A West Boca Raton homeowner says her efforts to receive a promised grant from the state to fix up her home keep facing one hurdle after another. Anne Bendel first contacted WPTV in May with an issue over her My Safe Florida Home grant being held up by paperwork from her insurance company. That issue was eventually cleared up, and My Safe Florida Home contacted her in May to say her status was complete. Then, a week later, representatives with My Safe Florida Home asked for more: a permit of completion for a large impact window. She provided it, but then came questions about dates. Now her application is back under review, and her hopes for any grant money toward the $8,000 she paid out of pocket are up in the air.

The My Safe Florida Home program has helped thousands of homeowners across the state with grants of up to $10,000 to fortify homes against storms and earn insurance discounts. But Bendel says she completed the work, got the permits, and had the insurance the program asked for. She feels the process is unfair, noting that it seems like when everything is done, they find some other task to request. WPTV has contacted the Florida Department of Financial Services in Tallahassee about Bendel's case and the status of her grant.

cards.headline: Alligator Alcatraz detainees scattered across U.S. as legal battles continue after facility closes
cards.teaser: Immigration attorney Richard Hujber says detainees from the controversial Everglades facility have been sent to facilities in Louisiana, Texas, New Mexico and as far as Tacoma, Washington.
cards.body:
Following the closure of the controversial detention facility in the Florida Everglades, immigration attorney Richard Hujber says detainees have been scattered across the country to facilities in Louisiana, Texas, New Mexico, and as far as Tacoma, Washington. The dispersal creates significant legal challenges for those fighting bond requests, Hujber explained, because different circuit courts across the country have varying laws and have denied bond requests in different circuits. With bond becoming out of reach for some detainees, Hujber says they face a difficult choice: continue fighting for residency or asylum, or self-deport. Gov. Ron DeSantis reported that roughly 21,000 people have been deported from the facility since it opened nearly a year ago.

For some families, the facility's closure brought relief. Anna Maria Hernandez's cousin was released just before Alligator Alcatraz shut down and is now under an order of supervision allowing him to drive, work and live in the U.S. Hernandez said her family lived every day wondering if their relative was safe. However, Hujber emphasized that the fight ultimately rests with the detainees themselves. "The hardest thing, Joel, is the families want to keep fighting," he said. "But it's the decision of the person doing the time." The Baker County facility in North Florida remains operational.

cards.headline: Fort Myers Mighty Mussels defeat Port St. Lucie Mets 6-2 with 4 home runs Saturday
cards.teaser: The Mighty Mussels slugged four home runs in a 6-2 victory over the Mets on Saturday.
cards.body: The Fort Myers Mighty Mussels posted a 6-2 win over the Port St. Lucie Mets on Saturday. The Mussels hit four home runs during the game. This was part of the ongoing series between the two Florida State League teams.

cards.headline: Former Haiti national team captain Jean-Marc Alexandre mentors youth soccer players in Boca Raton clinic
cards.body:
Former members of Haiti's national soccer team mentored young players in Boca Raton this week, just days after competing against Morocco. L'Union Fait La Force, a premier soccer development program run by former Haitian National Team members, hosted the clinic from June 25-28. Former team captain Jean-Marc Alexandre leads the organization. Alexandre is an Atlantic High School and Lynn University graduate who represented Haiti as national team captain and played for Real Salt Lake when the team won the MLS Cup in 2009. "The whole purpose of this camp is to give these kids a pathway to the youth national team, being that they're not living in Haiti, so we give opportunities to the next generation," Alexandre said.

Top-level young players including Nohe Chevry and Luis Etienne participated in the clinic. Chevry moved to Palm Beach County in 2022 with his family due to unrest in Haiti. He prioritized finding a local soccer program, which led him to L'Union Fait La Force. "It's a great opportunity to learn; they've been through all of the soccer stuff, pro contracts, so they can teach us, and it's really kind of them to do that," Chevry said. Etienne expressed similar appreciation for the program. "It's nice that they're giving us the opportunity to come out here and give us this opportunity to potentially get some exposure for the national team," Etienne said. Chevry's ambitions extend beyond the clinic: "I will take this to a high level, and my goal is to play in the World Cup and probably win it."

hero.headline: Florida Mango Festival returns Saturday to West Palm Beach Convention Center
hero.teaser: More than 75 vendors will showcase Florida-grown mango varieties, grafted trees, tropical fruits, and mango products at the air-conditioned Palm Beach County Convention Center.
hero.body:
The Florida Mango Festival takes place Saturday, June 27, at the Palm Beach County Convention Center, 650 Okeechobee Blvd., West Palm Beach. Organizers said more than 75 vendors will serve up local mango varieties, grafted trees, tropical fruits, and mango-themed products. Alex Salazar of Tropical Acres Farms told WPTV the indoor, air-conditioned venue offers an ideal setting for people to taste and learn about Florida-grown mangoes.

Festival co-organizer Vince Rogers previewed unique varieties including Fruit Cocktail, Orange Sherbet, and Pineapple Pleasure. He said Florida hosts more than 350 mango varieties far beyond what is typically available in grocery stores. Educational talks on home mango growing and grafting techniques will run throughout the day. Salazar will lead demonstrations offering tips for beginners and seasoned growers.

Additional features include an ID Your Mango booth, a scion exchange for online mango community members, and a master display of Florida's diverse mango cultivars. First pick ticket holders can enter at 9 a.m., with regular admission at 10:30 a.m. Garage parking is included with tickets, with limited availability. Paid public parking is available nearby north of Okeechobee Blvd. Tickets and information are available at floridamangofestival.com.

cards.headline: Peggy Adams Animal Rescue League shares hurricane safety tips for pet owners
cards.teaser: The Boca Raton shelter is urging South Florida residents to create a disaster plan for their pets before the next storm hits.
cards.body:
With hurricane season underway, Peggy Adams Animal Rescue League is urging South Florida residents to create a disaster plan for their pets. Dr. Alyssa Comroe, CEO of Peggy Adams, told WPTV the safest place for pets during a hurricane is right alongside their owners. The shelter's expert team recommends ensuring pets wear a collar with current identification and have an updated microchip registered with correct contact information.

Pet owners should introduce pets to a designated safe room ahead of time, such as a walk-in closet or downstairs bathroom, and conduct practice runs. An emergency kit should include a three-day supply of food and water in airtight containers, bowls, a sturdy carrier, bedding, towels, medications for two weeks, vaccination records, first-aid supplies, litter and box for cats, leashes, harnesses, cool packs, wipes, and waste bags. Peggy Adams recommends keeping a printed list of local pet-friendly shelters and hotels in an accessible place and maintaining recent photos of pets, ideally with their owner, for identification if separated. Conducting hurricane drills that include pets' daily routines of feeding, drinking water, and resting inside the safe room helps maximize comfort during an actual storm. Florida's hurricane season runs June through November.

cards.headline: George Snow Scholarship Fund awards record $7.5 million to 470 students in Palm Beach and Broward counties
cards.teaser: The Boca Raton nonprofit has distributed more than $45 million to over 4,100 students since its founding over 40 years ago.
cards.body:
The George Snow Scholarship Fund has awarded a record $7.5 million in scholarships and support services to 470 students across Palm Beach and Broward counties in 2026, according to President Tim Snow. Founded over 40 years ago, the Boca Raton-based nonprofit has distributed more than $45 million to over 4,100 students, making it the largest scholarship provider in Palm Beach County. The program bridges the gap between traditional financial aid and what students and families can afford by offering four-year commitments to ensure stability throughout college.

Vice President of Development Jay Brandt said GSSF services extend beyond financial assistance to include mentorship, professional development, and resources like the College Compass podcast. Wellington Community High School graduate Zya Chow received both the Royal Palm Hearing Aid Scholarship and the Davidowitz Family Caregiving Youth Scholarship and plans to attend Georgetown University. The Doyle-Whelchel Scholars Boutique, led by Scholar Services Coordinator Garvey Antoine, provides professional, formal, and casual wear for scholars to use during interviews, internships, and campus life. The boutique accepts donations of new or gently used clothing, footwear, and accessories.

cards.headline: SoFlo Market brings Independence Day celebration to Boca Raton City Hall Saturday
cards.body:
Founder Tatiana Freitas is organizing a free Independence Day edition of the SoFlo Market at Boca Raton City Hall on Saturday, July 4, from 11 a.m. to 5 p.m. at 201 West Palmetto Park Road. The celebration will feature a kids' parade, live DJ, and gourmet food from local vendors. The first 20 children through the gate will receive free gifts. Entertainment includes face painting, a foggy bubble station, mini golf, balloon twisting, handmade crafts, and desserts. The SoFlo Market's flamingo mascot will make a live appearance at the event.

Freitas told WPTV the market's mission is to uplift small local businesses and bring the community together. Boca Raton firefighters and police officers have been invited to attend. Freitas' son Kyle and husband Eddie are part of the organizing team. On-site generators will provide power for the event, and the market's Instagram, TikTok, Facebook and YouTube channels will feature behind-the-scenes clips and photos throughout the day. Free parking is available at City Hall. The SoFlo Market operates monthly, though Freitas says the Independence Day edition is always a standout event.

hero.headline: Byron Donalds adds $688,000 in one week while GOP rivals struggle to raise campaign cash
hero.teaser: The Republican gubernatorial front-runner collected nearly $253,000 for his campaign and $435,000 for his political committee, maintaining a massive fundraising advantage with nearly $66 million on hand.
hero.body:
With about 50 days remaining in the Republican primary to replace Ron DeSantis, Byron Donalds continues to vastly outpace his competition in fundraising. The gubernatorial front-runner added nearly $253,000 to his campaign account and $435,000 to his Friends of Byron Donalds political committee during the week ending June 19. This latest haul brings his total cash on hand to nearly $66 million, cementing his commanding position in the race. He has already booked a $20 million media buy for upcoming weeks, and even after spending that amount, he will maintain a substantial financial advantage over the other candidates in the field.

The contrast between Donalds and his opponents is stark. James Fishback raised only $4,825 to his campaign account and nothing to his Florida First political committee during the reporting period. As of June 19, Fishback had approximately $117,000 available to spend. During that same week, he spent more than $60,000 from his committee alone, including a payment to his running mate Sean Lozano. Jay Collins fared somewhat better, bringing in just over $11,000 to his campaign account and $1,500 to his political committee. However, Collins is burning through his resources quickly, with nearly $2 million from his committee going toward an ad buy in a single week. He currently has roughly $3.5 million available for the remainder of the race.

Former House Speaker Paul Renner continues to face serious fundraising challenges. He raised less than $30,000 to his campaign account for the second consecutive reporting period, along with $13,000 to his political committee. Renner has approximately $2.5 million to spend as of the June 19 closing date. Despite these modest figures, his resources still exceed those of Fishback, though he lags far behind both Collins and Donalds in available funds.

The candidates will not participate in a debate at Saturday's Florida GOP Sunshine State Showdown. Donalds and his allies contend that debates are unnecessary given the current state of the race. They argue that donors are unwilling to spend significant resources against what they describe as an inevitable nominee. While DeSantis and some members of the broader field have expressed interest in a debate format, it will not occur at this event. The fundraising numbers suggest that Donalds's assessment may have merit, as rival campaigns struggle to generate the financial support needed to mount a serious challenge to the front-runner.

cards.headline: DeSantis signs stablecoin framework and crypto kiosk fraud protections into Florida law
cards.teaser: Gov.
cards.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis signed three bills Friday that directly affect Florida's financial services sector and the treatment of money. CS/CS/HB 175 brings stablecoins under state regulation in line with the federal Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for U.S. Stablecoins Act, known as the GENIUS Act. The Office of Financial Regulation will determine whether an entity qualifies as a qualified payment stablecoin issuer by issuing a money services business license or, for trust companies, granting a certificate of approval. Under the law, stablecoins can be used for financial settlement with their value pegged at a fixed one-to-one rate of exchange with the U.S. dollar. The bill takes effect in October.

CS/CS/SB 1568 establishes the Florida Stablecoin Pilot Program within the Department of Financial Services, allowing applicants and licensees to voluntarily pay licensing, registration, application and renewal fees using approved stablecoins. The department will determine which stablecoins qualify based on strict financial safeguards, such as being fully backed by reserve assets worth at least $1 billion. DFS is authorized to maintain a state-designated digital wallet to convert stablecoin payments into U.S. dollars. HB 505 brings virtual currency kiosk operators under state money transmitter licensing rules, requiring registration with OFR and displaying fraud warnings on initial screens. Transaction limits are capped at $2,000 daily for new users and $10,000 for established customers.

cards.headline: Jay Collins and Paul Renner challenge Byron Donalds at Florida GOP event without debate
cards.teaser: Republican gubernatorial candidates who are not front-runner Byron Donalds delivered speeches criticizing the Naples congressman at the Republican Party of Florida's Sunshine State Showdown.
cards.body:
The Republican Party of Florida's Sunshine State Showdown did not feature a gubernatorial debate despite the lopsided race. After weeks of complaining they could not compete with Congressman Byron Donalds without a debate, Lt. Gov. Jay Collins and former House Speaker Paul Renner spoke in a room where Donalds was present. Second Lady Layla Collins gave extended remarks before her husband's speech, describing him as a man with moral compass and the best candidate to win a general election. She emphasized the importance of taking the fight to people and doing what is right rather than chasing headlines or social media clicks.

Lt. Gov. Collins directly criticized Donalds, comparing him to Charlie Crist and arguing that Republicans were being sold a familiar product. He detailed how Florida Democratic Chair Nikki Fried and her allies would use opposition research against Donalds in a general election, asking about character, stock trades, drug dealing, crime, money and influence, and every headline and disclosure. Renner largely avoided personal attacks, instead outlining his military service, prosecutor background, and tenure as Speaker as proof he would deliver results as governor. He positioned himself as the only candidate willing to fight, contrasting his approach against special interests controlling transactional politicians. Sen. Rick Scott reiterated his endorsement of Donalds before Donalds participated in a question and answer segment.

cards.headline: Attorney General James Uthmeier raises $1 million in one week, outpacing Democratic challenger by 40-to-1
cards.teaser: The Republican appointed by Gov. Ron DeSantis collected more than $1 million to his political committee, including a $900,000 check from the Republican Party of Florida.
cards.body:
Attorney General James Uthmeier reported raising $1.009 million to his Friends of James Uthmeier political committee and an additional $5,054 to his campaign account in the week ending June 19. A $900,000 check from the Republican Party of Florida comprised the majority of the haul, signaling party establishment support for the appointed incumbent. Other notable donors included The Southern Group and political consultant Alex Bruesewitz. Uthmeier now has more than $8 million in his political committee and nearly $1.1 million in his campaign account, totaling a war chest north of $9 million for a candidate who has never faced statewide voters.

Uthmeier, DeSantis' former Chief of Staff, was sworn in as the state's 39th Attorney General in February 2025 after Ashley Moody was appointed to the U.S. Senate seat vacated by Marco Rubio. At 37, he became one of the youngest attorneys general in the country and is now seeking his first full term in his own right. His Democratic challenger Jose Javier Rodriguez brought in $13,231, his weakest number in any filing to date. Rodriguez had roughly $215,000 on hand as of June 19, leaving him at better than a 40-to-1 cash disadvantage.

cards.headline: Agriculture Commissioner Wilton Simpson donates $3 million to Florida Senate GOP campaigns
cards.teaser: Simpson raised $449,400 in the week ending June 19 and donated $3 million to the Florida Republican Senatorial Campaign Committee while maintaining roughly $31 million on hand.
cards.body:
Agriculture Commissioner Wilton Simpson raised $449,400 between his campaign account and the Friends of Wilton Simpson political committee in the week ending June 19, but donated $3 million to the Florida Republican Senatorial Campaign Committee, which funds statewide efforts for the chamber he once led as president from 2020 to 2022. Simpson maintains roughly $31 million across his campaign account, political committee, the Florida Green PAC, Future Florida and the Home Grown PAC.

A fifth-generation Floridian who has operated a large-scale egg-laying operation in Pasco County for more than four decades, Simpson built a formidable political operation that helped flip the Agriculture Commissioner's office back to GOP control in 2022. He has since secured institutional support including an endorsement from President Donald Trump, backing from the Florida Farm Bureau and the support of 61 of the state's 67 sheriffs. His primary challenger Matt Taylor raised just over $6,000 during the week and has less than $69,000 on hand. Democrats Joey Mendoza Atkins and Don Prichard raised no money during the week, with Mendoza Atkins holding roughly $7,000 and Prichard holding less than $100.

cards.headline: Secretary of State Marco Rubio announces Israel-Lebanon framework agreement in Washington
cards.teaser: The framework establishes a process for dismantling Hezbollah and for Lebanon to regain territory taken by Israeli forces, with the U.S. committing $100 million in humanitarian assistance.
cards.body:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio joined Israel and Lebanon's ambassadors to the U.S. Friday to announce a framework agreement described as a first step toward peace following months of conflict between Israel and the Lebanese militant group Hezbollah. The agreement does not include Hezbollah and prompted one of the group's officials in Lebanon to warn of civil war. The State Department said the framework establishes a process for dismantling Hezbollah and for Lebanon to regain territory taken by Israeli forces as they battled the militant group. The U.S. will facilitate a newly created Military Coordination Group for Lebanon to implement the framework while committing $100 million in humanitarian assistance.

The agreement was signed in Washington by Yechiel Leiter, the Israeli ambassador to the United States, and Nada Hamadeh Moawad, the Lebanese ambassador to the United States. Leiter said the final destination of the framework is peace between the two countries and expressed hopes for normalized relations, stating Israel wants Hezbollah disarmed and dismantled so it can withdraw and Lebanon can regain full sovereignty. Moawad said the framework is a first step toward restoring Lebanese sovereignty and territorial integrity, securing a permanent cessation of hostilities, enabling people to return to their land and allowing all Lebanese to live in peace, security and prosperity.

hero.headline: Two people killed in head-on crash on Allapattah Road in Indiantown
hero.body:
Two people were killed in a head-on crash Saturday morning on Allapattah Road near Martin Highway in Indiantown. The crash occurred around 6:30 a.m. at 8113 SW Allapattah Road, also known as the Allapattah S-Curve, according to the Martin County Sheriff's Office.

Allapattah Road was blocked for about six hours while the Florida Highway Patrol processed the scene. The Martin County Sheriff's Office reported the crash and coordinated the road closure with state troopers.

The road reopened Saturday afternoon after investigators finished documenting the crash scene. The Florida Highway Patrol is handling the investigation into the collision.

The Allapattah S-Curve is a known dangerous section of roadway in western Martin County. The identities of the two people killed have not been released by authorities.

cards.headline: Vero Beach organization collecting supplies for Venezuela earthquake victims
cards.teaser: Latinas Nexus Network in Vero Beach is collecting essential supplies to ship directly to communities devastated by a massive earthquake in Venezuela.
cards.body:
Latinas Nexus Network in Vero Beach is hosting a Venezuela Earthquake Relief Drive to collect essential supplies for communities devastated by a 7.5 magnitude earthquake. The drive is organized by founders Lourana Navarro and Juliana Marino, along with Heidi Ramirez. Navarro, who was born in Venezuela and now lives in Vero Beach, said her family in Caracas is safe, but surrounding communities have lost everything. "Seeing the devastation, I know this is going to take decades to recover," Navarro said. The organizers are working with Global Empowerment Mission to ship collected supplies to Venezuela, ensuring 100% of donations are directed through verified humanitarian relief efforts.

Donations can be dropped off at 684 Old Dixie Highway in Vero Beach through Saturday, June 27, 2026, from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. The organizers are collecting powder Gatorade, non-perishable food, baby formula and food, diapers, baby wipes, feminine hygiene products, soap, shampoo, toothbrushes and toothpaste, rain boots, toilet paper, blankets, sleeping bags, flashlights and batteries, heavy duty garbage bags, first aid kits, bandages and gauze, hand sanitizer, cleaning supplies, face masks, nitrile gloves, and plastic bins with lids. To reach the organizers, contact Lourana Navarro at (954) 205-0700, Juliana Marino at (772) 913-0805, or Heidi Ramirez at (772) 213-2747.

cards.headline: Missing diver found dead on ocean floor near Fort Pierce Inlet
cards.teaser: A missing diver was found dead on the ocean floor approximately 6 to 7 miles north-northeast of the Fort Pierce Inlet Friday afternoon.
cards.body:
The U.S. Coast Guard Station Fort Pierce received a Mayday call over VHF Channel 16 at approximately 11:30 a.m. Friday regarding a missing diver. Following the distress call, the Coast Guard notified the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission, which immediately deployed four vessels to assist in the search. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit had independently monitored the Mayday call and was already en route to assist. A group of civilian boaters who were friends of the missing diver departed the Fort Pierce Inlet at approximately 1 p.m. to help with the search efforts. Aerial support was provided by both the Coast Guard and FWC.

Responding units made contact with the vessel involved nearly due east of Avalon State Park. At approximately 4:10 p.m., civilian divers entered the water and located the missing diver at the bottom of the ocean in approximately 55 feet of water, approximately 6 to 7 miles north-northeast of the Fort Pierce Inlet. The diver was recovered and pronounced deceased. The deceased was transported to Coast Guard Station Fort Pierce. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Criminal Investigations Division is conducting the investigation into the circumstances surrounding the incident, which remains ongoing.

cards.headline: Elise Elder sentenced for DUI manslaughter of Martin Drummond in Stuart
cards.teaser: Elise Elder was sentenced for DUI manslaughter in the death of Martin Drummond in Stuart.
cards.body:
Elise Elder was sentenced for DUI manslaughter in the death of Martin Drummond in Stuart. The sentencing took place Friday in Martin County.

Martin Drummond was killed in a crash involving Elder, who was driving under the influence. The case was prosecuted in Martin County Circuit Court.

hero.headline: Missing diver found dead on ocean floor near Fort Pierce Inlet
hero.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office is investigating the death of a diver who was found on the ocean floor approximately 6 to 7 miles north-northeast of the Fort Pierce Inlet. The U.S. Coast Guard Station Fort Pierce received a Mayday call on VHF Channel 16 at around 11:30 a.m. on Friday reporting the missing diver. In response, the Coast Guard contacted the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission, which quickly deployed 4 vessels to help with the search. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit had independently picked up the distress call and was already heading to the scene to assist with rescue efforts.

Friends of the missing diver who were boating in the area departed the Fort Pierce Inlet at approximately 1 p.m. to help with the search. Both the Coast Guard and FWC provided aerial support to aid responders in locating the diver. The responding units made contact with the vessel near Avalon State Park, positioned almost directly to the east. The coordinated effort between multiple agencies and civilian volunteers worked to cover the search area as quickly as possible.

At approximately 4:10 p.m., civilian divers entered the water and found the missing diver at the ocean bottom in approximately 55 feet of water. The diver was brought to the surface and pronounced deceased. The body was then transported to Coast Guard Station Fort Pierce.

The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Criminal Investigations Division has taken over the investigation to determine the exact circumstances surrounding the diver's death. The investigation remains ongoing as authorities work to understand what led to the fatal incident. The case highlights the dangers associated with diving operations and the importance of coordinated emergency response when divers go missing.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce Florida Highwaymen Museum featured in America 250 Road Trip
cards.teaser: The Florida Highwaymen Museum in Fort Pierce has been selected as a featured stop on the America 250 Road Trip celebrating the nation's 250th birthday.
cards.body:
The Florida Highwaymen Museum, which opened this year in Fort Pierce, is now a featured stop on the America 250 Road Trip, celebrating the nation's 250th birthday. The city announced the designation on its Facebook page this week. The museum celebrates 26 Black artists who began painting in the 1950s, creating bold, colorful landscapes of Florida's untouched beauty and selling them along the roadside when segregation kept them out of traditional galleries. Located at 1234 Avenue D, the museum is the nation's only one with exhibitions that include paintings from each of the 26 renowned Highwaymen artists.

The museum is currently operating on its summer schedule, open Saturday and Sunday from noon to 4 p.m. through July 31. The museum will be closed in August and reopen in September with a new exhibit. Fall and spring hours of operation will be expanded beginning September 1 through June 15.

hero.headline: Vero Beach group launches Venezuela earthquake relief drive at Old Dixie Highway location
hero.body:
Latinas Nexus Network in Vero Beach is organizing a relief effort to help Venezuelan communities devastated by a recent 7.5 magnitude earthquake. The organization, founded by Lourana Navarro and Juliana Marino with assistance from Heidi Ramirez, is collecting essential supplies to send directly to affected areas. Navarro, who was born in Venezuela, said her own family in Caracas escaped injury, but neighboring communities suffered catastrophic losses. "Where it was, there is a lot of my family there, so when I started seeing the magnitude and that it was a 7.5, I really got scared," Navarro said. She emphasized the scope of the crisis, noting that recovery will require many years and resources beyond what the country currently has available.

The organizers are working with Global Empowerment Mission, a verified humanitarian organization, to ensure that collected donations reach people in need. Marino stressed the importance of getting supplies to the most vulnerable populations. "From here, the only thing that I can do is do our best to come together and help them and find different resources so we can get it directly to the people and bring the help that they need," Marino said. The founders promise that 100 percent of donated supplies will go through established relief channels rather than being diverted elsewhere. Both organizers highlighted the most pressing needs among survivors. "I can tell you that the worst is the food and the place to sleep — to take a bath — they don't have that right now," Navarro said. Marino added that hundreds of thousands of people currently need assistance.

The relief drive is accepting donations from all community members, not exclusively from the Hispanic population. "We are asking not just the Hispanic community, we are asking everyone. They really need us," the founders said. Items needed include powder Gatorade, non-perishable food, baby formula and baby food, diapers of all sizes, baby wipes, feminine hygiene products, soap, shampoo, toothbrushes and toothpaste, rain boots, toilet paper, blankets, sleeping bags with batteries, flashlights and batteries, heavy duty garbage bags, first aid kits, bandages and gauze, hand sanitizer, cleaning supplies, face masks, nitrile gloves, and plastic bins with lids.

Donations can be dropped off at 684 Old Dixie Highway in Vero Beach through Saturday, June 27, 2026, between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. Those interested in contributing can contact the organizers directly: Lourana Navarro at (954) 205-0700, Juliana Marino at (772) 913-0805, or Heidi Ramirez at (772) 213-2747.
